sentences.text: The offences alleged against the petitioners are under Sections 294(b), 506 r/w 34 IPC and Section 120(o) of the Kerala Police Act.

2. The prosecution case is that due to the enmity of the accused persons towards the defacto Ammini K vs State Of Kerala on 16 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137476742/
2 complainant and her husband as they demanded back the money invested in the business conducted jointly, on several days since 15.7.2023, the 1st accused directly and through mobile phone intimidated the defacto complainant, abused her in filthy words and thereby they are alleged to have committed the aforesaid offences.
3. According the learned counsel for the petitioners, this is a false case foisted against the petitioners due to the difference of opinion between the defacto complainant and her husband.

entities.text: Ammini K vs State Of Kerala

sentences.text: Therefore, he prayed for quashing all further proceedings against the petitioners.
4. The petition was strongly opposed by the learned Public prosecutor.
Though notice was served on the defacto complainant/3rd respondent, she did not turn up.
In the FI statement, it is alleged that the husband of the defacto complainant paid some amount to the petitioners for investing in the business and also for purchasing a car.
When the said amount was not repaid, they preferred a complaint to the Peroorkada Police.
On 15.7.2023, they were summoned to the police station and arrived at a consensus.
Thereafter on several days, the 1st accused allegedly abused the defacto complainant and threatened her over telephone.
6. The allegations raised in the FIS are general in nature.

Not even a single specific instance with material particulars like date on which the petitioners allegedly abused and intimidated the defacto complainant and her husband, is disclosed in the FI statement.

In the absence of any specific allegation with material particulars like date and time of the alleged incident, no useful purpose will be served in continuing the proceedings against the petitioners as the same will only be an abuse of the process of the court.
7. Therefore, this Crl.M.C. is allowed.

All further proceedings against the petitioners in CC.No.511/2023 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate-IV (Mobile), Thiruvananthapuram,
arising out of crime No.1438/2023 of Peroorkada Police Station, is quashed.

Sd/-
C. PRATHEEP KUMAR, JUDGE sou.
